These deranged technicians hail from the most dangerous department in Underempire development, Crust Engineering. Their gear withstands temperatures in the thousands of degrees and even minor seismic reactions, and their specially modified drills can trigger magma breaches through the crust via phase resonance.

Most Skaven armies are made up of Clanrats — a great mass of ratmen cobbled together into a warrior caste. These Skaven belong to various clans, thousands of which are scattered across the underground empire's crypts, strongholds, and ever-present cave-cities. Among the various rat-kin, only lowly Skavenslaves and menial workers outnumber the Clanrats. When a warlord musters strength for battle, the Clanrats lead the charge, holding key positions along the battle line. They defeat their enemies in swarming hordes through overwhelming numbers and frenzied assaults. If a warlord can afford the price, and is on decent terms with Clan Skryre, a weapons team might accompany them. These devastating magical contraptions are viewed with suspicion by the Clanrats, who often suffer for the frequent technical mishaps that follow.

The underground empire runs on the labour of slaves. Skavenslaves do all the dirty and gruelling work — mining, tunnelling, growing food — and in years of poor harvest, they themselves become the food. Most of these rats are Skaven born into oppression, the lowest rung of the caste system. Whenever a rival clan is absorbed during civil war, this caste receives a fresh influx of new blood. Sometimes even non-Skaven wretches are pressed into slavery, though few of other races survive long under a ratman overseer's whip. In times of war, Skavenslaves are herded together to draw enemy fire or to overwhelm foes through sheer numbers. A common warlord tactic is to drive Skaven slaves ahead as living shields. As long as the losses are offset by gain, or serve to wear down the enemy before the next engagement, it matters little how many slaves die. The very best slaves might even manage to kill a few enemies — a windfall by any measure.

Night Runners are the most common warriors of Clan Eshin, though they remain as secretive as the rest of their clan. Trained for speed, Night Runners carry out swift raids ahead of the main Skaven force, clearing a path for the army to follow. Stealthy small units strike from the shadows to seize key strategic locations, while larger packs of Night Runners dash out to disrupt and slow the enemy's advance. Night Runners typically fight with paired blades, though some carry slings, raining shot upon enemy war machines or lightly armoured elite troops. Their signature tactic is to slip around an enemy flank and lure the foe into a hastily prepared ambush.

In Skaven society, most suspicious deaths and espionage are blamed on the malicious Clan Eshin. While these accusations are usually accurate, hard evidence is scarce. Such acts of sabotage are typically carried out by Clan Eshin's black-clad death squads — the Gutter Runners. Gutter Runners are trained in mysterious fighting techniques originating from the Far East, granting them speed and flexibility beyond that of ordinary beings, twisting and bending their bodies with unnatural suppleness. They also forgo cumbersome armour, relying instead on their ability to effortlessly dodge enemy blades and projectiles. Gutter Runner units are led by a 'Deathrunner' — a title usually bestowed upon those runners with the greatest potential to become assassins.
